lines.text: (lighthouse name), this is (ship 2 name) reporting position. We are reporting our presence approximately six nautical miles off (the lighthouse island) and twelve miles off the coast, over.
(lighthouse name), this is (ship 2 name) reporting position. Please copy. Over.
(lighthouse name), (ship 2 name) reporting position. Please copy once again. Over.
Copied, (ship 2 name) this is (lighthouse name) operator speaking. Over.
Copied, glad to hear from you. We have made several prior attempts to establish contact without acknowledgment. Over.
Understood, apologies for the delay. Please state your vessel name, current speed, and coordinates. Over.
Our vessel is (ship 2 name), reporting our presence approximately six nautical miles off (the lighthouse island) and twelve miles off the coast, current coordinates (coordinates). Over.
Copy that. The (lighthouse name) is (coordinates). Please state your present activities near these waters. Over.
We will be conducting whaling operations in the area of previously mentioned coordinates, over.

Understood. We would like to confirm whether your vessel holds a valid commercial whaling permit for operations in these waters, as well as your vessel’s intended duration to remain in the area. Over.
Affirmative, our vessel is operating under an authorized commercial whaling license, permit number AU-IWC-240497-972. Over.

Received, thank you for your cooperation. Be advised that there are other whaling vessels conducting similar commercial whaling operations in the surrounding waters. Please exercise caution and maintain a safe distance. Over.
Understood. Can you provide their approximate positions? Over.
At present one vessel, Sul Mare, last reported in the area yesterday evening, approximately four nautical miles northeast of your current position. Over.
Roger that, we will take this information into consideration. (ship 2 name) over and out.
Later that evening—the radio crackles back to life.
Copy, (lighthouse name), this is the Sul Mare captain. Over.
Copied, good evening captain. Over.
Evening, glad to hear from you again. We have an, ah, quite interesting inquiry regarding marine behavior in the surrounding area. Over.
Marine behavior…? In what nature? Over.

Around yesterday evening up to midnight, we experienced several unusual impacts against the underside of our hull. We suspect something may be moving beneath the vessel. Requesting information on any known marine activity in this area. Over.
Ah. Understood. Well, I’d say that the marine activity in these waters are quite lively; that’s the reason why your vessel is operating around these areas, yes? Over.
Right, but… we just didn’t expect constant intrusion during resting hours, is all. Over.

choice.text: Deny it and blame nocturnal creatures.
Ask more questions about what they heard.

lines.text: Well, rest assured that it’s not exactly unusual. Due to the depth of these waters, most of the creatures in these areas are nocturnal. Over.
Huh. Well, that’s somewhat reassuring, at least. Although their constant wailing has just been giving me headaches…
Well, thank you for the information. We wish you a quiet night, certainly more peaceful than ours… hah. Sul Mare over and out.
Radio is powered off.
(scoffing) Quiet night to you too.
Well, rest assured that it’s not exactly unusual. Due to the depth of these waters, most of the creatures in these areas are nocturnal. Over.
Huh. Well, that’s somewhat reassuring, at least. Although their constant wailing has just been giving me headaches…
(interrupted by radio static) Wailing?
Yeah… wailing. You know, like how whales do. Just these awful pitched singing all goddamn night. Over.
Well, whales tend to do that, yes. That’s how they communicate with each other. Over.

Right, but I’ve been in the industry since they overturned the ban back in 2267, y’know — I know what they’re like, how to hunt them down, make the killing strike… I know enough to tell ya that these aren’t their usual behaviors. Over.
Well. I guess I’m quite the contrary, then… I don’t know enough yet. I’m just the lighthouse keeper. Over.
Ah, well. (slight laugh) Don’t worry too much about it, sweetheart. For all I know these waters might just be haunted after all, that and your little island over there.
Maybe. Or maybe it’s just those animals you’re disturbing.
I beg your pardon?
… Apologies, it’s getting late. If there’s nothing else I can help you with, I’ll have to excuse myself to save battery power. Over.
Huh. Well, I’ll leave you to it. Don’t want the ghosts to come haunting you, too, huh?
No ghosts here, captain. Just the whales singing around.
(lighthouse name) over and out.
